requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module is prevented from loading now (immediate effect)
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed usb_storage was not loaded (cmd-5b3a92ee1cbd4c10). Executor created /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with both 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/false' directives (cmd-c1550aec45624884), then verified `sudo modprobe usb-storage` fails immediately with 'could not insert usb_storage: Invalid argument' (cmd-91ea1571c0604f20). Using the install-override directive (not just blacklist) ensures even explicit modprobe calls are blocked, not just udev auto-load — a robust implementation choice.

requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module remains blocked from loading after a reboot
requirements.summary: Executor checked that usb-storage was not embedded in the current initramfs (cmd-b5c7c565b04f4727), so no dracut rebuild was needed since /etc/modprobe.d is read at every boot. A real reboot was performed (cmd-5dea9433004143e5, reboot_ack=0), confirmed via a changed boot_id (636556ce... -> 64325cf5..., cmd-b28687dc29bb4e6d and global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). Post-reboot verification (cmd-05e0fe86b3ea4122) shows the blacklist file still present, usb_storage still not loaded, and modprobe still fails identically — directly demonstrating the block survives reboot.

requirements.requirement: Bounded disruption/restart is directly observed with pre-restart healthy baseline, disruption, and recovered healthy state (also load-bearing for this task's own reboot requirement)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart: boot_id 636556ce... and systemctl is-system-running='running' captured in the same call as the reboot issuance (cmd-5dea9433004143e5). During restart: three consecutive connection failures (timeout/reset) evidencing the node was actually down (cmd-912097d197874293, cmd-0a5bc7e3766b483d, cmd-fd2026b48d234101). Recovery: new boot_id confirmed (cmd-b28687dc29bb4e6d) and post-reboot systemctl is-system-running='running' with no failed services in the after_executor snapshot, showing full recovery.

overall_summary: The executor blocked usb-storage from loading immediately via a modprobe.d file combining 'blacklist' and 'install /bin/false' directives, verified the immediate effect, and then performed an actual node reboot that directly demonstrated persistence: boot_id changed, connection was interrupted during the restart window, and post-reboot checks confirmed the module is still blocked and the system is healthy ('running', no failed services). All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied with concrete before/during/after evidence, and no unnecessary or unreverted mutations were introduced.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was captured; longer-term persistence (e.g., across multiple reboots or kernel updates) is not directly observed, though the mechanism (modprobe.d, not initramfs-dependent) makes this a low risk.

The provider-wide restart evidence protocol appears fully covered by the same single reboot performed for the task itself (pre boot-identity, ack, post boot-identity, recovered state), so no separate protocol gap was identified.
